event_name: Molitor's De Lamiis published with witch woodcuts
significance: Ulrich Molitor's De Lamiis et Pythonicis Mulieribus (1489) was a skeptical legal-theological treatise that denied the physical reality of the witches' flight and sabbath while affirming the reality of demonic deception; the work is significant for its illustrated woodcuts — the first visual representations of the witch sabbath — and for representing a moderate skeptical position within the demonological mainstream.
source_method: Published primary source; modern analysis in Ankarloo and Clark, Witchcraft and Magic in Europe: The Middle Ages (2002) and Clark, Thinking with Demons (1997)
